transcript:
Header: 2026-03-04 17:00 UTC | Duration: ~56m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Sofia Lopez (Tidal Finance - Head of ML), Arjun Patel (Eng Manager), Liam O'Connor (Security), Nina Park (Data Scientist)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is maya from redwood, i have diego here with me, we'll run through the hosted api demo focused on chat and text generation, streaming, params and retries, any quick agenda items from your side?
[00:15] Sofia: thanks maya, yeah we're mostly focused on latency and cost, and also curious about streaming behavior for partial responses — for our embeddings+chat flow, we need low tail latency.
[00:28] Diego: awesome, that's exactly what we'll show. Quick note: we'll demo both the REST/SDK flows and show the console traces and a couple optimize suggestions. i'll kick off with a quick architecture slide — apologies if the deck auto slides are a bit off.
[00:45] Diego: so hosted api — simple REST endpoints, chat vs text endpoints, support for streaming via chunked responses, plus function/tool calling and structured output. in practice streaming will send partial tokens as they are generated, you can render incremental UI.
[01:10] Arjun: how often are those partial chunks sent? like every token, or buffered?
[01:18] Diego: great q — it's buffered by the runtime for efficiency, typically every 50-250ms depending on model and seq len, not literally per token. there's also a small TCP buffering effect on the client side.
[01:35] Sofia: and what about client-side retry behavior — if a stream drops mid-response, what's the right approach?
[01:42] Maya: yep so we recommend: if you lose a stream mid-response, treat the call as failed and kick off a fresh request with same conversation history; we show idempotency via a request_id header for your tracking; for long running streams you can checkpoint the partial tokens client-side but server doesn't support resuming a mid-generation stream today.
[02:05] Diego: demo time — i'll open the quickstart repo and run a node sdk example. (typing) here's a sample chat call: client.chat.create({model: 'redwood-large-001', messages, stream: true, max_tokens: 512, temperature: 0.2}) — you'll see we set stream true, low temp for stable answers.
[02:35] Diego: note on params: max_tokens controls generation budget, temperature/top_p influence randomness, and presence_penalty/frequency_penalty for repetitiveness. for safety we also have system-level filters and moderation hooks that you can opt into.
[02:55] Nina: do you have an example of streaming vs non-streaming latency numbers?
[03:02] Diego: yes, rough numbers from our verified profiles: 1.5-2x lower time-to-first-byte with streaming for the same prompt vs waiting for full generation. tail latency depends a lot on seq len and batching; we can include specific numbers in the benchmark spreadsheet.
[03:20] Maya: i'll share that benchmark sheet after this call — includes per-model p50/p95 for TTFB and total completion.
[03:28] Arjun: about batching — we worry about bursts causing higher latency if you rely on server batching — can we control batching or force low-latency mode?
[03:38] Diego: yes, you can set a qos flag on the route to prefer low-latency (less batching) or high-throughput (larger batching). Redwood will also respect dedicated capacity if you need predictable throughput. for hosted the default tries to balance cost and latency.
[03:58] Sofia: ok security questions — what about data retention and encryption?
[04:04] Maya: for hosted we offer configurable retention windows; encrypt at rest with customer-managed keys is available on Dedicated and Private; hosted uses our KMS and supports enterprise key integrations for Private deployments. i'll drop SOC2 scope and audit docs in the follow-up.
[04:28] Liam: we'll need SOC2 + SSO/SAML details and RBAC controls, also audit logs ingestion.
[04:36] Maya: yes, action item noted.
[04:40] Diego: back to retries — recommended pattern: client-side retry with exponential backoff for 5xx and transient network errors, don't retry on 4xx like invalid params. for streaming specifically, if you detect partial content and then a connection error, treat as failure and refire. sample pseudo: retry with jitter, max attempts 3, base 200ms.
[05:10] Diego: also watch for idempotency tokens for safe retries, and instrument request_ids for tracing in console.
[05:25] Diego: i'll switch to the console now — showing per-route dashboards: token-level cost, per-model latency breakdown, traces and sampling of responses, plus error analytics. (screen share) here you can trace a single request_id end-to-end and see where time was spent: network, model queue, decode.
[06:00] Sofia: can we see which requests were batched together?
[06:05] Diego: yes the trace shows batching groups and the batch size distribution; you can filter by latency and see hotspots. the optimize tab will suggest batching thresholds and when kv prefix caching would help.
[06:25] Diego: short demo of optimize: for chat workloads with repeated system prompts, prefix caching can save the KV cache and avoid re-encoding system tokens; optimize suggests caching rules and quantization profiles per model.
[06:48] Arjun: is quantization something you do in hosted? any impact on quality?
[06:55] Diego: we provide recommended quantization profiles that balance cost and quality per workload. hosted uses mixed precision paths; Optimize will show estimated token cost savings and expected quality delta from eval sets. good candidate models for 4-bit quantization depending on your quality tolerance.
[07:20] Nina: about evals — can we plug our prompts and run regression alerts?
[07:26] Maya: yes, Console/Evals supports prompt sets, regressions, and alerting on quality drift. we can set up a baseline with your test prompts.
[07:40] Diego: small note: sometimes transcripts or names in the console snapshot look garbled in auto-generated logs — ignore that, it's just OCR/transcription in the UI.
[07:55] Sofia: next, pricing — what's the cost model for hosted?
[08:02] Maya: hosted is usage-based per-token for generation plus per-embedding units where relevant. we have model-tiered pricing; i'll send the rate sheet. for production budgets we advise using Optimize to tune batch sizes and caching — typical customers see 20-40% unit cost reduction.
[08:28] Arjun: about burst protection — if our traffic spikes, do you throttle or drop?
[08:34] Diego: we have rate limits per key and per-account; when you hit those we return 429s and the recommended client pattern is exponential backoff with jitter. we also support reserved bursts in Dedicated.
[08:50] Maya: quick Q from my side — do you have an internal SLA requirement for tail p95?
[08:55] Arjun: we'd like p95 < 500ms for short prompts, p95 < 1s for typical chat completions.
[09:05] Diego: we can run a small benchmark POC to validate; for hosted we'll show p50/p95 and give guidance if you'd need Dedicated for stricter guarantees.
[09:18] Sofia: about data residency — we need EU region for EU customers, is hosted available in eu region?
[09:25] Maya: yes, we have hosted regions and can pin routes to region, or go Dedicated/Private for full isolation.
[09:35] Diego: switching back to code, here's a retry example in python: try: client.chat.create(..., stream=True) except TransientError: sleep(backoff); retry. and capture partial tokens if you want to present them but still persist final completion from server.
[09:58] Nina: any limits on message history size?
[10:04] Diego: server enforces model context window; we also have a route-level max_tokens_in_prompt param to protect costs. Optimize can detect long history patterns and suggest summarization or trimming strategies.
[10:25] Sofia: what about function calling? we want structured outputs to map to actions in our app.
[10:32] Diego: function/tool calling is supported, you define functions schema and the model will emit structured calls; streaming still works but function calls may return structured tokens that you parse.
[10:50] Arjun: for the POC, we want to test latency under concurrent users ~200 qps, and cost estimate.
[10:58] Maya: noted — action: diego will share a benchmark script that simulates concurrency and measures p50/p95/cost.
[11:10] Diego: demo wrap-up: summary of best practices — use streaming for improved time-to-first-byte and UX, set conservative retry policy with idempotency tokens, instrument request_ids and traces, use Optimize batching/caching for cost wins, and consider Dedicated for strict SLOs.
[11:35] Liam: last sec — security: audit logs and retention: how granular are logs, and who can access them in the console?
[11:44] Maya: RBAC in console supports role scoping; audit logs stream to your SIEM or can be retrieved via API; i'll include the exact schema in the follow up.
[11:58] Sofia: good — the deck + pricing will help internal approval.
[12:03] Maya: recap and next steps: i'll send pricing and SOC2/SSO docs; diego will share quickstart and benchmark script; let's schedule POC scoping week of 3/9. any objections?
[12:18] Arjun: none from engineering.
[12:21] Liam: security will review docs and follow up.
[12:24] Nina: thanks everyone.
[12:28] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up by Friday.
